static.aboutContent1: We are dedicated to providing unified, highly available AI API access services, helping developers and enterprises integrate top-tier AI models with ease.

static.aboutContent3: We continuously expand our supported model providers and model catalog, striving to become the go-to AI API aggregation platform for developers.

static.trustContent3: If you discover any security issues, please contact us through official channels. We commit to responding within 24 hours.

static.aboutIntro: {{brandNameEn}} is built as an AI API gateway for developers and enterprise teams that need lower integration overhead, clearer commercial operations, and more reliable delivery for multi-model products.
static.aboutSection1Body: We bring model access, unified authentication, usage-based billing, organization controls, and operational tooling into one platform so teams can spend less time on vendor differences and more time shipping product.
static.aboutSection1Item1: One OpenAI-compatible interface that reduces integration and switching cost
static.aboutSection1Item2: Built-in org, multi-tenant, subscription, and enterprise billing capabilities
static.aboutSection1Item3: A stronger operational foundation for routing, monitoring, and secure production delivery
static.aboutSection2Body: From indie builders to internal platform teams, {{brandNameEn}} fits organizations that need AI access to behave like a real product capability instead of an experimental side project.
static.aboutSection2Item1: Startups validating multi-model product strategy quickly
static.aboutSection2Item2: SaaS platforms that want unified procurement, billing, and access control
static.aboutSection2Item3: Enterprise engineering teams that care about auditability, security, and uptime
static.aboutSection3Body: We optimize for infrastructure that can be launched, operated, and improved over time. That means prioritizing stability, cost clarity, governance, and enterprise service over superficial marketing.
static.trustIntro: For an AI gateway, trust is earned through operational discipline, access control, and clear boundaries — not generic claims. Our trust posture is built around secure transport, permissions, auditability, and incident communication.
static.trustSection1Body: The platform is designed to reduce unnecessary exposure and keep model access, budgets, and API usage within defined business boundaries.
static.trustSection1Item1: Requests travel over encrypted channels to reduce transit risk
static.trustSection1Item2: Organizations, members, roles, and API keys can be governed at the platform level
static.trustSection1Item3: Quota controls and audit views help teams establish accountability internally
static.trustSection2Body: We treat security as part of the operating model, not a checkbox. That includes core-path monitoring, configuration controls, incident response, and customer-facing communication.
static.trustSection2Item1: Availability monitoring around the most business-critical service paths
static.trustSection2Item2: Audit visibility for important configuration, billing, and permission changes
static.trustSection2Item3: Status and announcement workflows for clearer incident communication
static.trustSection3Body: Whether you run an internal AI platform or a customer-facing SaaS product, {{brandNameEn}} is intended to support formal delivery workflows rather than short-lived demos.
static.trustCtaTitle: Need a more detailed trust or security discussion?
static.trustCtaBody: If your evaluation involves enterprise onboarding, permission models, or internal compliance review, we can walk through the platform in more detail.
static.legalIntro: Before teams move into formal adoption, they need a clear view of service boundaries, responsibilities, and information handling expectations. Our legal guidance is meant to make that process clearer, not heavier.
static.legalSection1Body: Before launch, customers should confirm that internal approvals, customer commitments, and model usage policies match the way the platform will actually be used.
static.legalSection1Item1: Using the platform means accepting the applicable Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
static.legalSection1Item2: Customers remain responsible for their accounts, keys, and usage behavior
static.legalSection1Item3: Sensitive or regulated use cases should go through enterprise review first
static.legalSection2Body: As product capabilities, regulation, and operating practices evolve, terms may change. We aim to surface meaningful updates through visible product or service channels.
static.legalSection2Item1: Material changes are communicated through visible announcement paths
static.legalSection2Item2: Continued use of the service means acceptance of updated terms
static.legalSection2Item3: Enterprise customers can align these updates with contract and support workflows
static.legalSection3Body: If legal, procurement, or security stakeholders need to review the platform, the enterprise process is the fastest path for clarifying service scope and deployment expectations.
static.newsIntro: This page tracks major product milestones, model coverage progress, partnership news, and operational updates so customers can understand where the platform is headed.
static.newsSection1Body: The news page is designed for both evaluators and existing customers who need business-relevant visibility into the platform.
static.newsSection1Item1: Major feature launches and enterprise capability updates
static.newsSection1Item2: Model catalog expansion and provider coverage changes
static.newsSection1Item3: Operational, support, or commercial policy updates
static.newsSection2Body: For production teams, platform updates influence engineering choices, procurement timing, and cost planning — so we aim to keep those updates useful and easy to track.
static.newsSection2Item1: Helps teams evaluate adoption timing and rollout scope
static.newsSection2Item2: Helps procurement and operations track pricing and capability changes
static.newsSection2Item3: Helps enterprise customers follow roadmap and support direction
static.newsCtaTitle: Want to stay close to platform changes?
static.newsCtaBody: For operating updates, pair this page with service announcements and the status page so product changes and runtime events stay clearly separated.
static.consultingIntro: If you are evaluating an AI API gateway, enterprise multi-tenant platform, or model access layer, consulting helps you decide faster whether {{brandNameEn}} fits the stage your business is in.
static.consultingSection1Body: To give practical guidance, we typically look at business goals, model requirements, traffic expectations, and delivery timelines together.
static.consultingSection1Item1: Which models you need today and how much switching flexibility matters
static.consultingSection1Item2: Whether you need org controls, budgets, member roles, or enterprise billing
static.consultingSection1Item3: Whether formal SLA, audit, or internal security requirements apply
static.consultingSection2Body: Consulting is not just a product demo. It is meant to help teams move more confidently from selection to pilot to launch.
static.consultingSection2Item2: Guidance on integration approach, billing model, and operating setup
static.consultingSection2Item3: Evaluation support for enterprise pilots and longer-term cooperation
static.consultingSection3Body: If you are already in product planning, procurement review, POC validation, or production migration, earlier consulting usually means less rework later.
static.announcementsIntro: Announcements are the central place for maintenance windows, policy changes, important updates, and other notices that can affect customer operations.
static.announcementsSection1Body: We aim to publish the changes that genuinely matter to evaluation, launch planning, and ongoing operation — not just minor internal movement.
static.announcementsSection1Item1: Maintenance windows and planned platform changes
static.announcementsSection1Item2: Updates to billing, model availability, or service policy
static.announcementsSection1Item3: Important feature launches and behavior changes
static.announcementsSection2Title: How customers should use this page
static.announcementsSection2Body: If your team depends on the platform in production, announcements and the status page should both become part of your normal operating information flow.
static.announcementsSection2Item1: Plan internal business windows before changes happen
static.announcementsSection2Item2: Track pricing and service rule changes earlier
static.announcementsSection2Item3: Keep engineering, ops, and support aligned on one source of truth
static.announcementsCtaBody: For live operational updates, use the status page. If you need stronger notification and response paths, evaluate the support plans.
static.supportPlansIntro: Our support plans are designed around business maturity, covering everything from self-service onboarding to enterprise-grade long-term operation.
static.supportPlansSection1Body: If your team already has engineering ownership and only needs dependable onboarding, launch, and issue handling, standard support is often enough.
static.supportPlansSection1Item1: Documentation, self-service configuration, and standard support paths
static.supportPlansSection1Item2: Response around platform features and common operational questions
static.supportPlansSection1Item3: A strong fit for developer teams and mid-size product rollouts
static.supportPlansSection2Body: Once your business relies on multi-team coordination, formal SLA expectations, budget governance, or procurement processes, enterprise support reduces operating friction significantly.
static.supportPlansSection2Item1: Priority response, issue coordination, and clearer change communication
static.supportPlansSection2Item2: More targeted guidance around org, multi-tenant, billing, and security setup
static.supportPlansSection2Item3: A better fit for organizations running AI as an ongoing business capability
static.supportPlansSection3Title: How to choose the right level
static.supportPlansSection3Body: The right plan usually depends on workload size, business criticality, internal ops maturity, and whether procurement or multiple stakeholders are involved.
static.serviceStatusIntro: The status page exists to keep engineering, operations, and business teams aligned when service conditions change, especially in production environments where scattered messages are not enough.
static.serviceStatusSection1Body: For production teams, status is not only about whether the platform is up. It is also about scope, progress, and expected recovery signals.
static.serviceStatusSection1Item1: Operational state of the API gateway, auth, billing, and other critical modules
static.serviceStatusSection1Item2: Incident scope, initial diagnosis, and remediation progress
static.serviceStatusSection1Item3: Post-recovery notes that help teams review and adjust
static.serviceStatusSection2Title: Make it part of your ops process
static.serviceStatusSection2Body: If the platform supports real customer workloads, your engineering, ops, and support teams should all use the status page as part of routine incident handling.
static.serviceStatusSection2Item1: Align internal and external communication faster during issues
static.serviceStatusSection2Item2: Reduce duplicated investigation and update overhead
static.serviceStatusSection2Item3: Support customer communication, troubleshooting, and SLA reviews
static.serviceStatusCtaTitle: Need a higher level of response and coordination?
static.serviceStatusCtaBody: If your business has tighter uptime or communication expectations, review announcements and support plans together.
static.playgroundIntro: The Playground is being shaped as a shared testing surface for product, operations, and engineering teams that want to compare models and validate prompts before formal integration work.
static.playgroundSection1Title: What it will help teams do
static.playgroundSection1Body: Compared with reading docs or writing immediate integration code, Playground is better for narrowing down model and prompt decisions quickly.
static.playgroundSection1Item1: Compare different models, parameters, and response styles faster
static.playgroundSection1Item2: Let non-engineering stakeholders participate in model evaluation earlier
static.playgroundSection1Item3: Create a more efficient validation step before API rollout
static.playgroundCtaTitle: Need to start with APIs now?
static.playgroundCtaBody: Until Playground is fully expanded, you can already evaluate the platform through the docs and API key workflow.
static.chatIntro: AI Chat will gradually support teams that want a fast way to validate model output, prototype internal assistants, and explore conversational business workflows.
static.chatSection1Title: What this direction is best for
static.chatSection1Body: This is intended to become more than a simple chat box — it is a lightweight workspace for model evaluation and scenario exploration.
static.chatSection1Item1: Internal knowledge and assistant scenario validation
static.chatSection1Item3: Early interactive prototyping for enterprise-facing use cases

enterprise.featureGroup1Title: Stabilize access, reliability, and security boundaries first
enterprise.featureGroup1Desc: Enterprise delivery is not just more models. It is a cleaner operating layer for model access, permissions, and reliability.
enterprise.featureGroup2Title: Then make governance, spend control, and collaboration work at team scale
enterprise.featureGroup2Desc: Once a team moves beyond pilots, the real questions become who can use what, how spend is controlled, and how incidents are handled together.
enterprise.fitTitle: Best for teams that are ready to ship AI as a real business capability
enterprise.fitSubtitle: If your priority has shifted from experimenting to launching, governing, and operating sustainably, the enterprise path will feel much more natural.
enterprise.fit1Desc: For teams balancing model coverage, customer delivery, access control, and commercial operations.
enterprise.fit1Point1: Reduce switching cost with one multi-model access layer
enterprise.fit1Point2: Add org, member, quota, and audit controls
enterprise.fit1Point3: Better suited to customer-facing AI delivery
enterprise.fit2Desc: For organizations serving multiple departments and centralizing budgets, permissions, and model access.
enterprise.fit2Point1: Use one API and one governance layer instead of repeated internal builds
enterprise.fit2Point2: Separate quotas and responsibilities by team or project
enterprise.fit2Point3: Align procurement, engineering, and operations around one system
enterprise.fit3Title: Teams entering procurement and formal evaluation

enterprise.fit3Point1: Turn ambiguous exploration into a clearer delivery path
enterprise.fit3Point2: Discuss SLA, support, and security requirements earlier
enterprise.fit3Point3: Reduce rework between PoC and full launch
enterprise.processTitle: From evaluation to launch, the path should stay simple
enterprise.processSubtitle: We keep the flow lightweight, but make the success-critical decisions explicit early.
enterprise.process1Desc: Understand your scenario, preferred models, traffic shape, and rollout pace, then decide whether governance, billing, or dedicated support is needed.
enterprise.process2Desc: Propose a more practical access, resource, and commercial plan instead of pushing a one-size-fits-all package.
enterprise.process3Desc: Validate the key business path first so engineering, product, and operations can see the real boundaries early.
enterprise.process4Desc: After launch, keep improving cost control, permissions, reliability, and support coordination.
enterprise.trustPoint3: Supports evaluation, pilot, and rollout alignment
enterprise.trustPoint4: Balances fast integration with controlled delivery

enterprise.heroCard3Title: Make the path from pilot to production much clearer
enterprise.heroCard3Desc: Reduce future rework across procurement, audit, and operations.
enterprise.solutionTitle: Start with the four things enterprise teams actually care about
enterprise.solutionDesc: In enterprise evaluation, the key question is rarely whether integration is possible. It is whether the system can be delivered, governed, and scaled cleanly.
enterprise.solutionRow1Desc: One interface layer reduces the cost of multi-provider integration.
enterprise.solutionRow2Desc: Routing and quota strategy reduce dependence on any single path.
enterprise.solutionRow3Desc: Manage members, projects, and quotas in the platform instead of with manual patches.
enterprise.solutionRow4Desc: Keep evaluation, integration, and optimization conversations more connected.
enterprise.solutionFootnote: Tell us what kind of business you run and what stage you are in, and we will start with fit and rollout path rather than a canned pitch.
enterprise.contactWhatToPrepareTitle: Helpful details to prepare before you submit
enterprise.contactCommitmentTitle: We care more about a clear recommendation than a longer form
enterprise.contactCommitmentDesc: If you do not need a heavy enterprise plan yet, we will tell you and suggest the lighter path.
enterprise.contactCommitmentItem1: We first judge whether enterprise is the right fit, rather than defaulting to the most complex plan
enterprise.contactCommitmentItem2: The conversation will focus on your scenario, scale, governance needs, and rollout timing
enterprise.contactCommitmentItem3: The more specific your context is, the more actionable our recommendation can be

homeAlt.whySubtitle: Not an extra layer. One less pile of chores.
homeAlt.whyCard1Desc: No separate signups, separate cards, separate keys for each provider. One account covers all.
homeAlt.whyCard2Desc: Usage settles together. No reconciling five platforms line by line at month end, no juggling different billing units.
homeAlt.whyCard3Title: Fails over when a model is down
homeAlt.whyCard3Desc: A comparable model takes over automatically. Your code stays the same, and nobody swaps configs at 3am.
homeAlt.whyCard4Desc: Shorter request paths and no network setup on your side. Timeouts and retries are handled server-side.
